newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel ends sharply lower against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel ends sharply lower against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel fell sharply against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Monday in very active trading following continued strong demand from the business sector, dealers said.
"Activity was very strong, but there was no evident reason for the decline," said Gideon Sadeh at Bank Leumi.
But another dealer said: "The business sector is closing positions before the end of the year. The trend may continue in the coming days."
Today, however, demand for dollars began fading when the U.S. currency reached 3.2750 shekels.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2730 shekels against 3.2530 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6641 shekels against 3.6459 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8804 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8610 on Friday and against the mark at 2.1219 shekels against 2.1189 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2740 shekels.
